key_insight: Retinal OCT models can identify biomarker presence yet struggle to localize findings; OCT-specific fine-tuning improved grounding F1 from 23.7% to 33.9%.
clinical_relevance: Reliable localization could help clinicians assess whether AI-reported retinal findings are supported by the image.
method: Introduced RetinaGroundBench: 815 OCT B-scans with 4,537 ophthalmologist-annotated boxes spanning 13 biomarkers and 8 diseases.
Proposed AggIoU to evaluate combined coverage when models fragment lesions across multiple predicted boxes.
Evaluated 27 open-source MLLMs and fine-tuned the 8B-parameter RetGrounder using OCT grounding and textual information.
evidence_signal: The best general-purpose model achieved 23.7% macro grounding F1, while RetGrounder reached 33.9%—a 43% relative improvement; biomarker-presence balanced accuracy reached up to 73%.
watch_item: Grounding performance remained limited, and these benchmark results do not establish clinical safety or readiness for deployment.
paper_title: A Visual Grounding Benchmark for Retinal OCT with Multimodal Large Language Models
